i0: **Quantifiers** tell us how many or how much: *all, most, some, none, each, every, both, either, neither*. Many can be used with or without ***of***: *most people / most of the people*.
i1: For *much, many, a few* and *a little*, see [Much, Many, A Few, A Little](/blog/grammar/much-many-a-few-a-little/). For *both… and* and *either… or*, see [Both… And, Either… Or](/blog/grammar/both-either-neither-not-only/).
qn-all-most-none.t: All, most, some, no: with or without of
qn-all-most-none.s: Use ***all / most / some / no*** + noun for things **in general** (*Most people like music*). Use ***all of / most of / some of / none of*** + ***the / my / these*** + noun, or a pronoun, for a **specific** group (*Most of my friends live here*).
qn-all-most-none.b0.0.1: ***All (of) the** children in my class are friendly.*
qn-all-most-none.b0.1.1: ***Most of the** people I know work hard.*
qn-all-most-none.b0.2.1: ***Some of the** shops in my street are closed.*
qn-all-most-none.b1: With a **pronoun**, always use *of*: ***most of them**, **some of us**, **all of it**, **none of you***.
qn-all-most-none.b2: ***All*** can drop *of* before *the / my / these*: ***all the** students = **all of the** students*. *Most* and *some* can't: ***most of the** students* (not *most the students*).
qn-each-every.s: ***Each*** and ***every*** + **singular** noun + **singular** verb. ***Every*** = all of a group, seen together (*Every student passed*). ***Each*** = one by one, separately (*Each child got a present*). Only ***each*** can be used with ***of*** or alone.
qn-each-every.b0.0.0: one by one: *Each player has a number.*
qn-each-every.b0.0.1: all together: *Every player wants to win.*
qn-each-every.b0.1.0: also for two: *She had a ring on each hand.*
qn-each-every.b1: Both take a **singular** verb: ***Every** room **has** a TV. **Each** of the rooms **has** a TV.*
qn-each-every.b2: For things that happen regularly, use ***every***: ***every** morning, **every** two weeks* (not *each two weeks*).
qn-both-either-neither.s: For **two** things: ***both*** = the one and the other (+ plural); ***either*** = one or the other (+ singular); ***neither*** = not one and not the other (+ singular). With ***of***: *both of / either of / neither of* + ***the / my / them***.
qn-both-either-neither.b0.0.2: *both of the children, both of them*
qn-both-either-neither.b0.1.2: *either of the days, either of them*
qn-both-either-neither.b0.2.2: *neither of the answers, neither of them*
qn-both-either-neither.b1: ***Neither*** is already negative, so use a **positive** verb: ***Neither** of them **came**.* (not *didn't come*). In negative sentences, use ***either***: *I **don't** like **either** of them.*
qn-both-either-neither.b2: After ***neither of / either of***, a **singular** verb is more formal and a plural verb is common in speech: *Neither of my parents **speaks / speak** English.*
qn-both-either-neither.b3: For **more than two**, use *all, any* and *none*: *None of my three brothers…*
x.qn-both-either-neither-s01: The one and the other: *both* (+ plural).
x.qn-both-either-neither-s03: Not one and not the other: *neither*.
x.qn-each-every-b03: *Each of the* + plural noun + singular verb.
x.qn-both-either-neither-b05: The one and the other: *both* (+ plural).
x.qn-both-either-neither-b06: Not one and not the other: *neither*.
